task_objective.description: Develop a mask-wearing adoption simulator that models individual compliance dynamics under information diffusion on a multiplex social network. The simulator should learn behavioural parameters (peer influence, information decay, risk perception sensitivity, broadcast intensity, temperature/noise) from observed agent-level trajectories using simulation-based inference (SBI) or gradient-free optimisation. The goal is to accurately reproduce observed daily mask-wearing rates and to generalise to counterfactual information campaigns or different network/topology settings.
simulation_focus: Calibrate decision and information propagation parameters from observed train trajectories using SBI or evolutionary search
Model coupled dynamics of mask-wearing state, information memory and broadcast campaigns on family/work/community network layers
Minimise discrepancy between simulated and observed distributions of daily mask-wearing (RMSE/MAE) as well as distributional metrics (Wasserstein) and transition fit
Support evaluation of interventions such as altered broadcast strength or modified peer influence weights to assess policy impact

data_files.train_data.csv: Agent-level training trajectories. Columns: day (int, 0-29), agent_id (int), wearing_mask (bool), received_info (bool). Contains 30 days × 100 agents (3,000 rows).
data_files.val_data.csv: Validation trajectories with identical schema as train_data.csv (days 30-34) used for early stopping/model selection.
data_files.test_data.csv: Test trajectories with identical schema (days 30-39) for final evaluation and intervention studies.
data_files.agent_attributes.csv: Static attributes per agent. Columns include age_group (categorical), occupation (categorical), risk_perception (float).
data_files.social_network.json: Multiplex adjacency lists keyed by agent id. Each entry contains lists for family, work_school, community neighbours (agent ids).
data_files.metadata.json: Dataset metadata: description, population size, day ranges for train/val/test splits, random seed, notes on broadcast intervention day and baseline parameters.

RMSE_daily_rate.description: Root Mean Squared Error between simulated and observed daily mask-wearing rates on validation/test windows.
RMSE_daily_rate.interpretation: Lower values indicate better fit to aggregate adoption curve. Values below 0.1 mean good agreement.

MAE_daily_rate.description: Mean Absolute Error between simulated and observed daily rates.
MAE_daily_rate.interpretation: Provides more interpretable deviation in percentage points.

Wasserstein_distribution.description: 1-Wasserstein distance (Earth Mover's Distance) between simulated and observed distributions of daily rates or agent-level samples.
Wasserstein_distribution.interpretation: Captures distributional mismatch beyond mean errors.

Transition_fit.description: Average absolute error between simulated and observed transition probabilities (P01, P11, P10, P00).
Transition_fit.interpretation: Assesses dynamic consistency of entering/leaving mask-wearing state.

Broadcast_memory_accuracy.description: Optional metric: MAE between simulated information memory and observed received_info prevalence.
Broadcast_memory_accuracy.interpretation: Measures how well information diffusion is captured.
